prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: EO mission; ground segment plans, acquires, operates, produces, archives, controls access (excludes spacecraft, launch, user processing); security: least privilege, strong auth, segmentation, continuous audit. Mission Control Center (Bluebell): real-time ops, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule/routing policy, routine-ops authority boundary; elevated access only with approved shift role, time-limited need; contact = readiness, monitoring, closure; sends constraints to Mission Planning System (MPS), receives command preparation package. MPS: uses Laser Retroreflector Window only within approved interval. Spacecraft Operations Team (SOT): console lead declares pass status, authorizes commands, pauses on telemetry mismatch; uses Antenna Deicing Notice, Pass Replay Packet (anomaly reconstruction); receives maneuver recommendation package above conjunction threshold; leads spacecraft-safety triage. Escalation console>discipline lead>mission management. Anomaly classified by safety, command authority, data custody, service continuity, user commitments. Possible fault: preserve command state, no discretionary commanding. Stack queued only with MCC+SOT concurrence. Command Validation Gateway (Osprey): shall validate stacks; shall reject unapproved edits, missing provenance, expired config, out-of-window; accepts Star Tracker Mask File only if integrity, config ID, approval match security baseline; consults Telemetry Ingest Service, Orbit Determination Engine (produces retroreflector window). Cybersecurity Desk: reviews exceptions, public interface changes, privileged access daily; coordinates on suspicious auth/data movement/tampering; receives Security Exception Ticket from Ground Network Manager (Juniper; leads antenna/link/site triage). Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral): sends mask file; ephemerides to MCC, MPS, PPF (validity, frame, time, use); orbit quality changes to archive queue first. Flight Dynamics Team: uses Doppler Residual Report, produces Ephemeris Delta Note; assesses orbit/timing. Network Control System (Lantern): enforces routing, logs changes; sends MCC antenna status, link config; keeps last validated routing. Payload Calibration Team: Calibration Patch Bundle; reprocessing requests; product-integrity triage. Product Quality Service: quality flags, Product Hold List, records reprocessing reasons. Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse): Primary/Backup Clusters. Long Term Archive (Granite): admits after PPF package, metadata, checksums; preserves replaced versions; Storage Watermark Snapshot daily; catalogue (baseline, times,

New part:
S213: During triage, operators preserve volatile logs, current configuration state, operator console history, and relevant message identifiers before restarting services or changing routing.
S214: Evidence is stored in write-protected case storage with a chain of custody entry that identifies the collector, collection time, source system, and reason for capture.
S215: Forgehouse must quarantine suspect input and derived output when product lineage cannot be proven during an active anomaly investigation.
S216: Cedar suspends automatic schedule publication when a security or continuity anomaly could invalidate contact commitments or conflict with manual recovery actions.
S217: Continuity modes are declared by the Mission Control Center after consultation with the affected technical leads and are recorded with the operational objective, expected duration, and exit criteria.
S218: In monitor-only mode, command release is stopped, telemetry reception continues where safe, and engineering teams focus on stabilizing observability and protecting evidence.
S219: In essential-service mode, the ground segment prioritizes spacecraft safety contacts, time-critical telemetry capture, core orbit support, and protection of unrecoverable payload data.
S220: Primary Processing Cluster can pause nonessential production queues and reserve compute capacity for validated recovery runs from known-good inputs.
S221: If site degradation persists, processing work is transferred to Backup Processing Cluster only after input custody, software baseline, and operator authorization have been verified.
S222: Cross-site failover is coordinated through Ground Network Manager so that antenna allocation, network routing, firewall state, and contact schedules remain consistent.
S223: North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna are placed in the recovery plan according to current availability and the spacecraft contact priority.
S224: Long Term Archive remains the custody reference during degraded operations, and any delayed ingest or publication is reconciled before normal service status is restored.
S225: User Services Portal communicates confirmed service impacts in operational terms and avoids publishing speculative root cause information before the incident lead approves release.
S226: Recovery is accepted only when command authority is verified, telemetry and product flows are reconciled, security monitoring has returned to the approved baseline, and responsible teams have signed the incident record.
S227: Routine mission service begins only after the operational readiness review confirms that ground procedures, staffing rosters, monitoring views, and escalation paths are under configuration control.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
